claims.text: First: which sequence is it? T1-weighted: fat is bright and fluid is dark; best for normal anatomy and fat
claims.quote: For example, fat appears bright (high signal intensity) on T1-weighted images and relatively dark (low signal intensity) on T2-weighted images; water and fluids appear relatively dark on T1-weighted images and bright on T2-weighted images. T1-weighted images optimally show normal soft-tissue anatomy and fat

claims.text: T2-weighted: fluid is bright; best for showing abnormalities such as tumors, inflammation and trauma
claims.quote: T2-weighted images optimally show fluid and abnormalities (eg, tumors, inflammation, trauma).

claims.text: STIR: suppresses the fat signal so other tissues with high water content stand out
claims.quote: Short T1 inversion recovery MRI can suppress signals from fat allowing enhancement of other tissues with high water content.
claims.locator: Short T1 Inversion Recovery MRI of the Whole Body (image caption)

claims.text: What MRI is used for here Joints and tumors: MRI is preferred over CT for suspected musculoskeletal tumors and internal joint derangement
claims.quote: MRI is preferred to CT when soft-tissue contrast resolution must be highly detailed (eg, to evaluate intracranial or spinal cord abnormalities, inflammation, trauma, suspected musculoskeletal tumors, or internal joint derangement).

claims.text: Certain fractures: MRI can show hip fractures accurately in patients with osteopenia
claims.quote: MRI can provide accurate images of hip fractures in patients with osteopenia.

claims.text: Marrow: MRI helps sort marrow abnormalities into metastases versus nonmalignant lesions
claims.quote: characterizing bone marrow abnormalities as metastases versus nonmalignant lesions

claims.text: Pelvis: MRI adds to ultrasound to characterize adnexal masses and stage uterine tumors
claims.quote: MRI supplements ultrasound to further characterize adnexal masses and to stage uterine tumors.

claims.text: Bone infection If radiographs are equivocal or symptoms are acute, CT and MRI are the imaging of choice and show nearby infection such as epidural abscess
claims.quote: If radiographs are equivocal or symptoms are acute, CT and MRI are the imaging techniques of choice to define abnormalities and reveal adjacent infections, such as paravertebral or epidural abscesses, or infected facet joints
